label: copy phase: fed-back a (esp. a followed by b) from mid-sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is a (97% of activation mass; b inputs give a small remainder). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on a first occurrence of a token. It is concentrated at recall_idx 3-4, i.e. when the a sits at original position 2-3, and is more common in long sequences (L=8-9). Magnitude depends strongly on the output: the largest activations come when the token being output after a is b (bigram ab, e.g. x y a b ... -> [a:1.0]). Output a (aa) is next strongest; other outputs give weak activations. Most a inputs in the copy phase stay silent (in_tok==a alone has precision ~0.07), so the gating condition beyond the a-then-b context is not fully captured. Recording a, recall_idx>=3, output in {a,b} gives dev F1 0.51, precision 0.68, mass recall 0.61.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: a, b, -, 3, 2, m; least: k, t, 0, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: b, a, g, 0, j, q; least: 2, o, -, c); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=9 & t=13.
